Ch XI (23 Oct): 35 stills by Ian — Lucy's good days, the mother who opened the window, Van Helsing's despair, the Zoo keeper and the tall stranger with the pointed beard, Bersicker's escape and return, Renfield's knife, Seward's train, and Lucy's last memorandum (the wolf at the window, her mother's death, the drugged maids, the specks in the moonlight). Hands checked at full size before placing. Ch XII (23 Oct): 48 stills by Ian — the silent house at Hillingham, the saw at the kitchen window, mother and daughter on the bed, the drugged maids, the fire, Quincey's blood, the paper, the sunset vigil; Mina's letters from Exeter (the toast, Mr Hawkins's death, the asylum report); and Lucy's death — Arthur at her side, the kiss forbidden, peace, Van Helsing's stern 'It is only the beginning'. Two 'kiss' versions dropped (Van Helsing appeared to kiss Arthur). Ch XIII (23 Oct): 39 stills by Ian, with the moon placed as it really stood over London, 20–25 Sept 1893 (waxing gibbous rising in the late afternoon, full on the 25th): Lucy laid out, the garlic and crucifix, the will, Arthur's farewell; the funeral, Piccadilly at sunset with the rising moon and the tall stranger, Jonathan's terror, the telegram; Van Helsing's laughter, Hampstead Heath under the full moon, the far white lady, the child found at dawn. Piccadilly (cues 90–97) redone in daylight from Stoker's description: Rotten Row's empty chairs, the girl in the cart-wheel hat outside Giuliano's with the moon rising, the Count close (pointed black beard, red lips, a straight nose at Ian's request), Jonathan's terror, the hansom. Ch XIV (24 Oct): 37 stills by Ian — Van Helsing in Exeter (his letter, his arrival, the typed journal, the pledge, the cathedral close), Jonathan restored (supper, the handshake, the train, Exeter at dusk under a waning moon), and Van Helsing's lesson to Seward (the Westminster Gazette, the lecture, Charcot, the tortoise and the bat, 'it was Miss Lucy').
